consumer: The frontend's detection/targeting logic asking 'can the avatar see this specific monster right now?', whose engine-authoritative answer is the boolean returned by Creature::sees( that monster ) — the engine EVALUATES a computed yes/no.
scope: A single avatar-to-this-monster visibility predicate (range + light + line-of-sight + concealment from the avatar's vantage), not the whole export window and not a sprite-draw/remembered-tile view.
decisive_source: src/creature.cpp::Creature::sees — its body computes the live see/no-see boolean from rl_dist range, light, here.sees line-of-sight, vehicle-rotation obscuring, hallucination and concealment checks, returning the authoritative visibility result.
divergence: A monster standing in the export window but behind an opaque wall (or in darkness / hidden by crouch-coverage): raw window/position state (Excerpt 3 in_export_window) lists it as present, but Creature::sees returns false — reporting 'visible because it is in-window' is exposed wrong.
